turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
“Over the past two weeks my skin has slowly turned yellow, and I’ve had generalized itching. I’ve also had decreased appetite and lost about 6.3 kg, with pale stools and very dark urine.”

Have you had any abdominal pain—especially in the right upper abdomen—or fever/chills?
Have you had any abdominal pain—especially in the right upper abdomen—or fever/chills?

“No, I haven’t had fever or chills, and I haven’t had new right upper abdominal pain recently. The last time I had significant upper abdominal pain was about three years ago, and it was managed with IV fluids, NSAIDs, and dietary changes.”
Have you noticed any nausea or vomiting?
“No, I haven’t had nausea or vomiting. I’ve mainly just had the yellow skin, itching, poor appetite, pale stools, and very dark urine over the past two weeks.”
Do you have any history of gallstones, pancreatitis, hepatitis, heavy alcohol use, or prior abdominal surgery?

“I don’t have a known history of gallstones, pancreatitis, or hepatitis, and I haven’t had abdominal surgery. I did drink 1–2 beers daily for about 40 years, but I’ve been abstinent for the last three years.”
Have you had any imaging or blood tests done for this jaundice, and if so, what were the results?
“I haven’t had any imaging or blood tests yet for this, and I’m not sure what evaluations have been done.” “I did recently notice my urine has been very dark and my stools much paler than usual.”
Have you noticed a painless lump or fullness in the upper abdomen, or has anyone told you your gallbladder or liver feels enlarged?

“I haven’t noticed any painless lump or a specific fullness in my upper abdomen, and no one has told me my liver or gallbladder feels enlarged. The main things I’ve noticed are the yellowing of my skin, the widespread itching, the pale stools, and the very dark urine.”
How old are you, and what sex were you assigned at birth?
“I’m 72 years old, and I was assigned male at birth.”
Do you smoke, or have you smoked in the past?
“Yes, I’ve smoked about a pack of cigarettes daily for around 50 years.”

[DDX] Pancreatic head adenocarcinoma causing obstructive jaundice, Cholangiocarcinoma, Choledocholithiasis causing extrahepatic biliary obstruction, Ampullary carcinoma, Benign biliary stricture

Painless progressive jaundice with pruritus, dark urine, pale stools, anorexia, and significant weight loss in a 72-year-old man strongly suggests obstructive cholestatic jaundice, with malignancy most likely. Heavy smoking and weight loss particularly raise concern for pancreatic head cancer. Cholangiocarcinoma and ampullary carcinoma are also important considerations. A stone is still possible, especially with prior upper abdominal pain years ago, but is less likely without current pain or fever.

This needs urgent evaluation with:
- Liver panel: total/direct bilirubin, ALP, GGT, AST/ALT
- CBC, CMP, INR
- Lipase
- RUQ ultrasound
- Contrast CT abdomen/pelvis focused on pancreas/biliary tree, or MRCP depending on availability
- Likely GI referral for ERCP/EUS if obstruction is confirmed

Red flags requiring prompt in-person care: fever, worsening jaundice, confusion, severe abdominal pain, vomiting, or bleeding.
